title: Pediatric Cardiac Arrest — Numbers Card (PALS)
sources: 2025 PALS — Pediatric Cardiac Arrest Algorithm; Pediatric Bradycardia with a Pulse; Pediatric Tachycardia with a Pulse (AHA-aligned)
Critical Vector — Pediatric Code Blue (numbers card, every dose cross-checked vs current PALS, July 2026)
Pediatric Drug Dose Chart, Queen's University Department of Anesthesiology, 2021 (dextrose, magnesium, lidocaine cross-reference)
AHA / American Red Cross CPR tempo guidance (100–120/min)

changelog.change: Initial entry — the PALS 'numbers to remember' card: 1-2-4 rule, metabolic-emergency doses, CPR mechanics, and the bradycardia/SVT/shockable/unstable-tachycardia quick card. Converted from the CV Pediatric Code Blue guide.

purpose: The recall-level numbers for a paediatric resuscitation — arrest and peri-arrest drug doses, defibrillation and cardioversion energies, and CPR mechanics — in one card. Every dose is weight-based; compute from the measured or length-tape weight and respect the adult-equivalent single-dose caps. Full per-drug detail and infusions are on the linked drug cards.

rows: max 1 mg per dose; repeat q3–5 min
min none in current PALS; 0.1–0.5 mg per dose; may repeat once
PALS range 0.5–1 J/kg first attempt, then double
up to 10 J/kg or the adult dose
Dextrose (5 mL/kg D10, or 2 mL/kg D25)
VF / pulseless VT (may repeat up to 15 mg/kg, max 300 mg per dose)
Torsades or severe bronchospasm; over 15–30 min; max 2 g
hyperkalaemia, hypocalcaemia, hypermagnesaemia, CCB overdose — central line preferred

items: Compression rate 100–120/min. Depth: ⅓ of the AP chest diameter (~4 cm infant, ~5 cm child).
Infant technique: two-thumb encircling (two rescuers) or two fingers / heel of one hand — the old two-finger-only wording is gone.
Compression : ventilation 30:2 single rescuer, 15:2 with two rescuers; once an advanced airway is in, ventilate 1 breath every 2–3 s (~20–30/min) with continuous compressions.
Swap compressors every 2 minutes. Any 100–120 BPM song works as a metronome (Stayin' Alive ~104, Dancing Queen ~101, Uptown Funk ~115).
Pulse/rhythm check every 2 minutes; keep pauses < 10 s.

rows: CPR if HR < 60 despite oxygenation/ventilation → epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg; atropine 0.02 mg/kg for vagal / AV block
Vagal manoeuvres → adenosine 0.1 then 0.2 mg/kg rapid push
Synchronized cardioversion 0.5–1 J/kg, double if repeated
Defib 2 → 4 J/kg; epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg q3–5 min; amiodarone 5 mg/kg or lidocaine 1 mg/kg after the 3rd shock
CPR + epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg early, q3–5 min; hunt the Hs & Ts (add Hypoglycaemia for children)
Calcium chloride 20 mg/kg or calcium gluconate 60 mg/kg; then shift (insulin/dextrose, salbutamol, bicarbonate)

body.text: Every number here is per-kg — get a weight before the arithmetic (measured, parent-reported, or the length tape / weight zone). Watch the single-dose ceilings: epinephrine 1 mg, atropine 0.5 mg, adenosine 6 then 12 mg, amiodarone 300 mg, magnesium 2 g.

buildNote: peds-tool, kind reference (no keywords/related per schema). Numbers card converted from CV Pediatric Code Blue; cross-checked against 2025 PALS. Cardioversion and magnesium stated as the PALS ranges rather than the rounded single values used in the source. Infusions and full per-drug detail live on the resus drug cards.
